hypotheses.justification: The statement is still true at n = 0. VeroneseRing 𝒮 0 = ⨁ j, 𝒮 (0*j). The element zeroVariable 𝒮 = of 1 (zeroUnit 𝒮 1) lies in component 𝒮 0 1. By aeval_zeroVariable_surjective (GradedRings/VeroneseZero.lean, no hypotheses on n, hgen or nontriviality), Polynomial.aeval (zeroVariable 𝒮) from (component 𝒮 0 0)[X] onto VeroneseRing 𝒮 0 is surjective. So Algebra.adjoin (component 𝒮 0 0) {zeroVariable 𝒮} = ⊤, and since {zeroVariable 𝒮} ⊆ component 𝒮 0 1, the adjoin of component 𝒮 0 1 is also ⊤. A trivial S is covered too, because the surjectivity argument is unconditional. The proof changes by splitting on n = 0 versus n > 0 (Nat.eq_zero_or_pos). The n = 0 case uses the surjectivity above via Algebra.adjoin_le and the range of aeval. The n > 0 case keeps the existing proof, where hn is only a local fact used by eval_mem_adjoin and inclusion_injective. hgen is still needed, since at n = 1 the statement is equivalent to it.
